statement: The 2024 financial audit covered Pike Township's financial position and results of operations for 1 January through 31 December 2024.
locator: Independent Auditor's Report, PDF pp. 3-7

statement: For 2024, SBOA issued an adverse opinion under U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and an unmodified opinion on the regulatory-basis financial statement.
locator: Independent Auditor's Report, Opinions, PDF pp. 3-4
notes: The dual opinion reflects two accounting frameworks; the adverse GAAP opinion is not a finding of fraud.

statement: The 2024 supplemental report describes compliance procedures under Indiana Code 5-11-1 and reports instances SBOA considered noncompliance; the procedures were not designed to identify every noncompliance instance.
locator: Transmittal Letter, PDF p. 3
notes: The report should be read with the 2024 financial-statement audit.

statement: SBOA states that official responses included in the 2024 supplemental report were prepared by the auditee and were not verified for accuracy.
locator: Transmittal Letter, PDF p. 3
notes: All response and corrective-action assertions are therefore kept separate from auditor findings.

statement: SBOA found internal-control deficiencies that contributed to noncompliance in 2024.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Internal Controls - Compliance, PDF p. 4

statement: The 2024 control criteria cite Indiana Code 5-11-1-27(e) and Indiana's Uniform Internal Control Standards, requiring controls to provide reasonable assurance of compliance and safeguarding of resources.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Internal Controls - Compliance, PDF p. 4

statement: In a sample of 18 employees for 2024 payroll testing, one employee received two salary increases totaling $4,000 that were not authorized by the union contract, salary resolution, or another policy.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Compensation and Benefits, PDF p. 4
notes: Administrative finding; no criminal conduct or intent is inferred.

statement: SBOA's additional review identified multiple employees who received similar unauthorized increases in 2024 totaling $20,000.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Compensation and Benefits, PDF p. 4
notes: The report's wording does not clearly state whether $20,000 includes or is additional to the sampled $4,000; the dataset does not add the amounts.

statement: For compensation, SBOA cited Indiana Code 36-6-6-10(c): the township legislative body fixes employee compensation and must establish it in a salary schedule; compensation must also be authorized by a labor contract, ordinance, resolution, or schedule unless otherwise authorized by law.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Compensation and Benefits, PDF pp. 4-5

statement: For 2024, SBOA requested a mileage log but one was not provided, and the auditors found no documentation showing that a log had been maintained during the audit period.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Vehicle Usage, PDF p. 5
notes: A missing record is established; improper trips are not inferred.

statement: SBOA cited Indiana Code 36-6-4-4 and 36-6-8-3, which restrict township-vehicle use to authorized official duties and require the trustee to maintain a log of use.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Vehicle Usage, PDF p. 5

statement: The Trustee's 2024 response said officials had not understood that additional pay for expanded duties required salary-resolution approval, that the practice was discontinued until approval, and that future changes would be reviewed and included in the salary resolution.
locator: Official Response, Pike Township Trustee, PDF pp. 6-7
notes: Auditee assertion reproduced by SBOA; SBOA expressly did not verify official responses.

statement: The Trustee's 2024 response said the vehicles were a shared pool and logs had not been consistently maintained; it said a trip log was placed in each vehicle and would be retained and monitored.
locator: Official Response, Pike Township Trustee, PDF pp. 6-7
notes: Implementation and effectiveness were not audited in this report.

statement: The Township Board's response accepted the compensation and mileage-log findings and requested examination of compensation practices it said may predate the 2024 audit period.
locator: Official Response, Pike Township Board, PDF pp. 8-12
notes: The claimed earlier period lies outside SBOA's stated 2024 scope and is not treated as an auditor finding.

statement: The Township Board's response discussed gift cards and a reimbursement as though they were a separate audit finding, but no such finding appears in the 2024 supplemental report's table of contents or Audit Results and Comments section.
locator: Official Response, Pike Township Board, PDF pp. 8-12, compared with report contents and PDF pp. 4-5
notes: Preserved as an unresolved response/report discrepancy, not represented as an SBOA finding.

statement: The 2025 financial audit covered the Township's financial position and results of operations for 1 January through 31 December 2025.
locator: Independent Auditor's Report, PDF pp. 3-8

statement: For 2025, SBOA again issued an adverse opinion under U.S. generally accepted accounting principles and an unmodified opinion on the regulatory-basis financial statement.
locator: Independent Auditor's Report, Opinions, PDF pp. 3-4
notes: The adverse GAAP opinion is not evidence of criminal intent.

statement: The 2025 supplemental report used the same compliance-procedure scope and limitation as the 2024 report and again stated that auditee official responses were not verified for accuracy.
locator: Transmittal Letter, PDF p. 3

statement: SBOA found internal-control deficiencies that contributed to noncompliance in 2025.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Internal Controls - Compliance, PDF p. 4

statement: The 2025 Annual Financial Report grant schedule omitted part of Medical Assistance Program reimbursements from Indiana FSSA under Assistance Listing 93.778, understating the schedule by $1,022,949.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Annual Financial Report - Grant Schedule, PDF p. 4
notes: Reporting understatement; not an assertion that funds were missing or misused.

statement: For the grant-schedule finding, SBOA cited Indiana Code 5-11-1-4(a), which requires annual reporting of receipts, disbursements, indebtedness, and other requested financial information.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Annual Financial Report - Grant Schedule, PDF p. 4

statement: In a sample of 16 employees for 2025 payroll testing, one employee received two salary increases totaling $4,000 that were not authorized by the union contract, salary resolution, or another policy.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Compensation and Benefits, PDF pp. 4-5
notes: Administrative finding; no criminal conduct or intent is inferred.

statement: SBOA's additional review identified multiple employees who received similar unauthorized increases in 2025 totaling $20,000.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Compensation and Benefits, PDF p. 5
notes: The wording does not clearly state whether $20,000 includes or is additional to the sampled $4,000; the dataset does not add the amounts.

statement: For 2025, SBOA again requested a mileage log but one was not provided, and no documentation showed a log had been maintained during the audit period.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, Vehicle Usage, PDF p. 5
notes: Repeated missing-record finding; no inference about the nature of any vehicle trips.

statement: Federal finding 2025-001 classified controls over preparation of the Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards as a material weakness and reported the same $1,022,949 understatement; proposed audit adjustments were accepted and made.
locator: Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs, Finding 2025-001, PDF pp. 13-17
notes: The adjustment corrected the schedule for the audit; it does not by itself verify future controls.

statement: Finding 2025-001 cites Indiana Code 5-11-1-27(e), 2 CFR 200.303, 2 CFR 200.1, 2 CFR 200.508, 2 CFR 200.510(b), and Indiana Code 5-11-1-4(a) as applicable control and reporting criteria.
locator: Finding 2025-001, Criteria, PDF pp. 13-16

statement: SBOA attributed the 2025 SEFA error to the absence of a system for compiling and reviewing federal-award information; the report says the Trustee was unfamiliar with the schedule because no federal audit had occurred during the Trustee's term.
locator: Finding 2025-001, Condition and Context / Cause, PDF pp. 13-17
notes: This is the auditors' stated cause for a reporting-control finding, not an inference of intent.

statement: The 2025 federal audit reported no federal award findings or questioned costs, issued an unmodified opinion on compliance for the major Medicaid Cluster program, and stated that Pike Township was not a low-risk auditee.
locator: Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs, Summary of Auditor's Results and Section III, PDF pp. 13 and 17
notes: Separates the financial-reporting material weakness from major-program compliance results.

statement: The corrective action plan for finding 2025-001 says the Fire Department would forward Medicaid communications to accounting, the departments would reconcile EMS deposits, accounting would be copied on reimbursement notices, and receipts would be tracked for future annual reports.
locator: Corrective Action Plan, Finding 2025-001, PDF p. 18
notes: Management's plan; SBOA did not audit its future effectiveness in this report.

statement: The 2025 corrective action plan lists immediate implementation and an anticipated completion date of 31 December 2026.
locator: Corrective Action Plan, Finding 2025-001, PDF p. 18
timeBasis: Anticipated completion date stated in plan; midnight UTC is a date-only placeholder and the date is prospective relative to the report.
notes: Planned completion is not evidence of completion.

statement: The Trustee's 2025 response said the omitted Medicaid amount resulted from coding and identification problems and described new reporting and reconciliation steps; it repeated the compensation and vehicle-log corrective statements.
locator: Official Response, Pike Township Trustee, PDF pp. 6-8
notes: Auditee explanation and planned correction; not verified by SBOA.

statement: The Township Board's 2025 response emphasized recurrence of compensation and mileage-log findings and again discussed the gift-card matter that is not listed as an SBOA finding in the released supplemental reports.
locator: Official Response, Pike Township Board, PDF pp. 9-15
notes: The Board's characterization is preserved as a response, not promoted to an auditor finding.

statement: The reports establish recurring documentation and authorization deficiencies across 2024 and 2025, but they do not establish criminal conduct, intent, or that township funds were stolen.
locator: Audit Results and Comments, PDF pp. 4-5; scope limitations at PDF p. 3
notes: Analytical limit based on the administrative audit's findings and stated scope.

statement: Future evidence is needed to determine whether the promised payroll-authorization, vehicle-log, and federal-reporting controls were implemented and operated effectively after the audit periods.
locator: Corrective Action Plan, PDF p. 18, read with finding recommendations
notes: Analyst recommendation for verification; the source establishes the plan, not subsequent operating effectiveness.
